s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
key_facts: The patient is a toddler with a 2-month history of skin eruption
The eruption began with multiple round red patches that slowly increased in size
The patient has a medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
The patient was treated with griseofulvin and clotrimazole without improvement
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
The patient is currently taking acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
Scattered café au lait macules are present on the back
Histopathology showed a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
The white blood cell count is 76,400/µL

Histiocytoid sweet syndrome with systemic involvement

Histiocytoid sweet syndrome with systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's medical history of juvenile xanthogranulomas and presence of café au lait macules

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multisystem involvement with skin, bone, and possible hematologic abnormalities

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Emperipolesis and positive staining for CD4 and CD163, although less likely given the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histiocytic infiltrate with uncertain lineage, possible relationship to other histiocytic disorders

raw.rationale: The patient's histopathology results showing a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, along with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Additionally, the patient's medical history of NF1 and the presence of café au lait macules are also associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology results do not match the typical findings of juvenile xanthogranuloma, which usually shows a mixture of mononuclear cells and multinucleated giant cells.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical presentation are not typical for Erdheim-Chester disease, which usually affects adults and presents with systemic symptoms and bone lesions.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology results do not show the characteristic emperipolesis (phagocytosis of lymphocytes) seen in Rosai-Dorfman disease.

rejected.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The patient's immunohistochemical staining profile is more consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis than indeterminate cell histiocytosis, which typically lacks expression of CD1a and langerin.
